name: Amanemu
positioning: Aman's ryokan-inspired onsen resort beside Ago Bay in Ise-Shima, Japan
best_for: Travelers who want an onsen and spa stay by Ago Bay
Guests who want to visit Ise Grand Shrine and meet Ama divers

facts.text: Amanemu is a ryokan-inspired onsen resort beside Ago Bay, amid the forested hills of Ise-Shima.
The cedar villas at Amanemu were designed by Kerry Hill.
The spa has a thermal spring garden with daybeds.
Spa treatments incorporate local and seasonal ingredients, including pearl powder, seaweed, and herbs used in traditional kampo therapies.
Wellness facilities include an outdoor swimming pool, steam rooms, a yoga studio and a fitness centre.
Guests can take a half-day visit to the Naiku (Inner Shrine) of Ise Grand Shrine, followed by a stroll through the Oharaimachi district.
Amanemu offers a private sunset cruise on Ago Bay.
Round-trip transfers from Kashikojima Station are included.
Daily breakfast and dinner are included, excluding beverages.

highlights.text: The villas' humble construction pays homage to Ise Jingu, Japan's preeminent Shinto shrine.
The spa has two private onsen bathing pavilions.
The signature Ise Jingu shrine breakfast is enjoyed overlooking Ago Bay and served in a handcrafted white wooden box.
The Ama Hut Lunch offers a charcoal-grilled seafood lunch with stories from Ama divers and a visit to an Ama hut.
The Sai-shi Mai ritual dance is performed at dusk on the Sunken Terrace against the backdrop of Ago Bay.

considerations.text: The property is very secluded and a taxi is needed to get off property.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires additional travel time from major cities.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing reflecting Aman's exclusive positioning.

sources.title: Amanemu - Hotel Review, Conde Nast Traveler
